newsitem.title: USA: Service Corp. board to meet on Loewen bid.
newsitem.headline: Service Corp. board to meet on Loewen bid.

text.p: The stock of funeral giant Loewen Group Inc. of Canada rose again Tuesday on anticipation that archrival Service Corp. International would launch a hostile takeover bid on the eve of Loewen's listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

The board of directors of Houston-based Service Corp., the No. 1 funeral home and cemetery operator in North America, was to meet Tuesday to consider its next step after No. 2 Loewen's rejection last week of an unsolicited stock offer of $2.8 billion, or $43 per share.
Industry experts expected an announcement from Service Corp. after the stock market closed.
"I think there will be a tender offer. Service Corp. certainly has been very tenacious and disciplined about these kinds of things in the past," said Lynn Detrick of Williams MacKay Jordan & Co. Inc.

Loewen stock, which rose $1.25 to $41.875 Monday on the belief that Service Corp. would sweeten its offer, gained 37.5 cents by afternoon to $42.25 on Nasdaq. Service Corp. stock fell 62.5 cents to $29.625 on the NYSE.

Service Corp. publicly disclosed its interest in Loewen on Sept. 17. Eight days later, Loewen flatly rejected the unsolicited bid, saying the offer was inadequate and that it intended to remain independent.
In recent days, industry analysts and takeover traders have speculated Service Corp. may launch a bid as high as $48 per share.
"If you know that you're not going to have the board's endorsement, you sweeten (the offer) and take it to the shareholders," one takeover trader said.
Although a combined Service Corp.-Loewen would hold only about 10 percent market share in the highly fragmented North American funeral industry, antitrust issues already have emerged.

Last week, Florida officials said they were investigating antitrust implications associated with the Service Corp. offer. Service Corp. has acknowledged that it may have to divest some properties if the deal were consummated.

Since Service Corp. disclosed its interest, Loewen has announced two acquisitions as part of its strategy to expand market share. Both companies have been aggressively buying small, privately held funeral industry companies.

Loewen officials are expected to be in New York Wednesday to celebrate the listing of the company's stock on the New York Stock Exchange, where it will trade under the symbol "LWN". The company announced in early September that it would switch to NYSE from Nasdaq to reflect the company's growth.
Loewen stock also trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange and the Montreal Exchange.
Loewen is based in the Vancouver, British Columbia, suburb of Burnaby.
